topology_reasoning.what_it_is: Two identical single-mode strip waveguides. Each enters straight at a port, S-bends toward the other, runs parallel across a central coupling region at a minimum edge-to-edge gap, then S-bends apart and exits straight. The silhouette is mirror-symmetric top/bottom about the horizontal midline (y=1.5um).
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: In the coupling region the two guides are close enough that their evanescent fields overlap; the even/odd supermodes beat, transferring optical power from the input guide to the neighbor. Fractional power transfer = sin^2(kappa * L_eff), where kappa (per-length coupling) is set by the gap and the S-bend approaches contribute additional coupling (effective length > the straight coupling_length).

function_defining_knobs.coupling_gap: edge-to-edge separation of the two cores in the coupling region -> sets kappa (coupling strength). Smallest gap in the whole device.
function_defining_knobs.coupling_length: length of the parallel coupling region -> sets total accumulated coupling / power-transfer ratio.
function_defining_knobs.wg_width: waveguide core width -> mode confinement / single-mode operation; also sets kappa via mode overlap.
function_defining_knobs.sbend_length: horizontal length of each S-bend approach -> adiabaticity / bend loss and the extra coupling accumulated on the bends.
function_defining_knobs.bend_offset: vertical displacement of each S-bend (half the change in center-to-center separation from coupling region to port) -> sets how far the guides fan out to the ports.
function_defining_knobs.input_length: straight section length at each of the 4 port stubs.

measurements_from_target_um.note: extracted by vertical-column band scan on component.png using calibration scale (88 px/um x, 149 px/um y)
measurements_from_target_um.flat_input_extent_um: ~1.0 (centerline constant y at x=0.0 and x=0.9)

topology_reasoning.parametric_model: Each guide centerline = straight(input_length) -> cosine S-bend(sbend_length, bend_offset) -> straight(coupling_length) -> mirror. Built as a gf.Path polyline extruded to wg_width on layer (1,0). Cosine profile y=y0+(y1-y0)*(1-cos(pi*u))/2 gives zero slope at both ends (smooth, kink-free junctions). Total length = 2*input_length + 2*sbend_length + coupling_length = 18 um. Half center-to-center at coupling = (coupling_gap+wg_width)/2; at ports = that + bend_offset.
topology_reasoning.hand_fit_check: cosine model with input_length=1.0, sbend_length=6.5, coupling_length=3.0, bend_offset=0.70 reproduces the measured top-guide centerline (0.326->1.023 um from top) to within ~0.03 um (~4 px) across all sampled columns.

iterations.change_made: Initial cosine-S-bend directional coupler built from image measurements (6 top-level function knobs). gds bbox 18.0x3.02 um.
iterations.diff_study: Thin (2-4 px) edge fringes only. Systematic patterns: (a) ~0.011 um port-separation overshoot on the input/output straights (mine slightly more spread than target); (b) small +0.027 um bump where the cosine S-bend approaches the coupling region.

iterations.change_made: Reduced bend_offset 0.70 -> 0.689 to correct the measured +0.011 um port-separation overshoot (from column-by-column centerline comparison of raster vs target). Improved input/output straight alignment; precision/recall balanced to 0.986/0.986. gds bbox 18.0x2.998 um.
iterations.diff_study: Remaining residual is the S-bend tail: target descent matches a cosine exactly for u<=0.55 of the bend, then approaches the coupling region ~0.04 um more gently than any symmetric easing. Capturing it needs an asymmetric-bend knob that trades middle-fit for tail-fit.

stopped_because: IoU 0.9724 >> 0.85 target after 2 iterations. Further gains require abandoning the clean 6-knob cosine parameterization for an asymmetric-bend pixel-fit; deliberately kept the clean parametric model (better for downstream spec-retargeting) as the honest best.
gds_write_note: device.py writes with with_metadata=False so the device cell (directional_coupler) stays top-level. Otherwise kfactory wraps it in a $$$CONTEXT_INFO$$$ cell that becomes the sole top-level cell; _layer_area/_layer_bbox skip $$$ cells and would read 0 area / error (also breaks Phase-B footprint checks). compare_absolute is unaffected (IoU identical 0.9724).

knob_verification.most_important_function_knob: coupling_length (sets accumulated coupling / power-transfer ratio; the knob that changes total material area, so it is the one an area-based check can measure)

verify_knob_response_coupling_length.interpretation: The knob DOES move real geometry: +5 um coupling_length grows layer-(1,0) area by 6.60 um2 = 2*wg_width*5 (BOTH waveguides extend). verify_knob_response is MZI-shaped: its delta_length check is structurally N/A for a symmetric/balanced coupler (both arms equal by design -> no imbalance for a symmetric knob to move), and its single-guide area expectation is half the real two-guide growth (area_ok passes only with width_um=2*wg_width). Neither boolean-false is a knob failure.

direct_area_sweep_tool_independent.verdict: PASS - perfectly linear, exactly 2*wg_width; coupling_length moves real geometry as physics predicts.

knob_verification.note_on_coupling_gap: coupling_gap is the other primary function knob (sets kappa). In this parameterization changing it translates the guides apart without changing their length or area, so an area/length-based check (verify_knob_response) is blind to it by construction; its geometric effect is the min edge-to-edge gap, verified visually against the target (0.30 um) at IoU 0.9724.
